items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: I didn't know him. I didn't know any of -- very few of the lyric writers that I know because they

ctx.x: You hadn't been in the band very long a tune called "Sophisticated Lady" was recorded, and I find it rather interesting that in Benny Ashland's discography, which was published in Scandanavia, that on February 15th, 1933, you hadn't been in the band even a year then, there was a recording session at which "Sophisticated Lady" was recorded. And Ashland lists the composers as Ellington, Hardwick, Brown and Mills. I notice on record labels that that isn't the list at all. They say Ellington, Mills and Parish. Who…

Well, that's one of those everybody jumps in and helps out, but mainly I had a theme which I played all the time which is the first eight bars. And Otto Hardwick played the -- the release, and I went back to the first eight bars. That was the basic tune of "Sophisticated Lady". And I got the terrific check of $15.00 for -- for writing "Sophisticated Lady"
